_guide: Lines the game builds sentences from. Lines live in named groups; the game asks a group for a line.
A line is either plain text, or { "text": ..., "when": {...}, "weight": 2 }.
Inside the text:
{crew}          the crew member in this scene (shows their name). {place}, {item}, {biome}, {weather}, {time} work the same way.
In crew lines, {crew} is one crew member (or you). {crew.role} is their profession, {crew.trait} their trait, {crew.wear} what they wear, {crew.gear} what they carry, {ship} the ship's name.
{crew.name}     a part of it. {Crew} = capital first letter.
{crew.they} {crew.them} {crew.their} {crew.theirs} {crew.themself}   pronouns that follow the person.
{crew.they} {crew:laughs|laugh}   after a pronoun: 'she laughs', 'they laugh'. After a name just write the verb: '{Crew} laughs'.
{a:item}        adds 'a' or 'an': 'a brass lantern', 'an old map'.
{@smell}        drops in a line from the group called smell, so you can build sentences from small pieces.
[soft|quiet|still]   picks one of these at random.
when (optional): the line is only used when everything in it matches.
"biome": "desert"        only on deserts.  ["desert", "salt"] = any of them.  "!rain" = anything but rain.
"temp": ">0.6"          numbers: above 0.6 (or "<0.3" for below). temp, water, life go from 0 to 1.
"crew.tags": "nervous"  a part of something: here, the crew member's trait tags.
weight (optional): 2 = picked twice as often, 0.5 = half as often.
Groups with the same name in different files are joined, so you can make a new file in content/ for your own lines
(add it to CONTENT_FILES in js/boot.js). Try lines in tools/text-preview.html.
Biomes are often plural ("rust plains"), so don't put a verb or "a" straight after {biome}: write "the light over the {biome} turns", not "the {biome} turns".
crew_pair lines have two people: {crew} and {other} (both work like {crew}). bond is how many study sessions they've shared: "bond": "<4" for near-strangers, ">15" for old friends.
postcard: the caption on a postcard of {world}, written by {crew} (lines work like the others).

arrive: The ship settles down on the {biome}. Everything is [quiet|still|hushed] for a moment.
{Place} looks [smaller|bigger|stranger] than it did from orbit.

arrive.text: At {time} the light over the {biome} turns [pink|gold|violet]. {@smell}
Rain drums on the hull. Nobody is in a hurry to step outside.
Frost creeps across the windows as soon as the engines go quiet.
The air shimmers with heat. {Crew} fans {crew.themself} with a map.

smell: The air smells of [rain on stone|burnt sugar|old books|cold metal].

smell.text: Something here smells like salt and lightning.

crew_notice.text: {Crew} jumps at a noise, then laughs at {crew.themself}.
{Crew} turns over every stone in sight. Most of them are just stones.
{Crew} says this planet is too [cold|loud|purple] and then writes three pages about it.

item_moment: {Crew} holds up {crew.their} {item} to get a better look.

item_moment.text: {Crew}'s {item} catches the light. Something out on the {biome} seems to notice.
{Crew} pulls {crew.their} {item} a little tighter against the wind.
{Crew} lights {crew.their} {item}, and the dark steps back a little.
{Crew}'s {item} keeps {crew.them} dry while everyone else gets soaked.

ship_life: {Crew} spends the session reorganising {crew.their} bunk. It looks exactly the same afterwards.
{Crew} writes a long letter to someone back home and doesn't send it. Not yet.
{Crew} [hums|whistles|sings] something old in the corridor. Nobody asks what it is. Everybody knows the tune by the end.
{Crew} falls asleep in the observation deck with a book open on {crew.their} chest.
{Crew} makes tea for everyone. It's slightly too strong, which is how the {ship} likes it.
{Crew} spends an hour watching the stars slide past the window and calls it work.

ship_life.text: {Crew} polishes {crew.their} {crew.gear} until {crew.they} can see {crew.their} own face in it.
{Crew} plays a few notes on {crew.their} {crew.gear}. The engines seem to hum along.
{Crew} sketches the corridor, the galley and the back of somebody's head.
{Crew} pours everyone something warm from {crew.their} {crew.gear}.
{Crew} fixes a squeaky hinge with {crew.their} {crew.gear} and then fixes three more out of momentum.
{Crew} pulls {crew.their} {crew.wear} a little tighter. The ship is cold tonight.
Someone compliments {crew}'s {crew.wear}. {Crew.they} {crew:pretends|pretend} not to be pleased.
{Crew} tunes the engines by ear and declares them "happy".
{Crew} cooks something new. It is purple. It is delicious. Nobody asks.
{Crew} runs the same test three times and gets three different answers. {Crew.they} {crew:looks|look} delighted.
{Crew} flies a little loop just because the stars look nice from upside down.
{Crew} talks a passing freighter into swapping a bag of apples for a song.
{Crew} checks everyone's temperature. Prescription: more naps.
{Crew} tells the story of the last world over dinner, and makes it sound even better than it was.
{Crew} waters the little plants in the galley and tells each of them it's doing well.
{Crew} redraws the last map from memory. It's better than the real one.
{Crew} paints a tiny planet on the galley door. Then another. It's turning into a solar system.
{Crew} practises one song over and over until the whole crew can hum it.
{Crew} jumps at the sound of the coffee machine, then pretends {crew.they} meant to.
{Crew} grumbles about the noise, the cold and the soup, then helps with all three.
{Crew} naps through an entire course correction. Twice.
{Crew} finds a snack nobody knew the ship had.
{Crew} tells a joke so bad that the whole galley groans, then laughs for ten minutes.
{Crew} labels the spice rack. And the labels. And the drawer the labels came from.
{Crew} spends the session at the window, watching nothing in particular, very happily.
{Crew} spends the evening at the telescope, naming craters on a moon nobody else can see yet.
The record player is going, and {crew} is dancing in the corridor like nobody's watching. Everybody's watching.
{Crew} waters the little garden in the hold and talks to each plant by name.
{Crew} curls up in the reading nook with a book about a world nobody has found yet.
{Crew} cooks something slow on the big stove, and the whole ship smells like home.
{Crew} wins three games in a row at the game table and is no longer allowed to pick the game.
{Crew} sways gently in a hammock in the hold, half asleep, half watching the stars.

ship_life: {Crew} finds a note under {crew.their} pillow that just says "good luck today". Nobody owns up to it.
{Crew} spends the session teaching the ship's computer a new joke. The computer does not laugh. {Crew} says it is thinking about it.
{Crew} reorganises the spice rack by colour. The cook is not consulted. There are consequences.
{Crew} sits by the window and counts stars until losing count, then starts again, happily.
{Crew} fixes a squeaky door that has squeaked since the ship was built. The silence is almost unbearable.
{Crew} makes everyone a cup of something warm without being asked.
{Crew} finds an old photo stuck behind a panel: a crew from long ago, grinning, on this same ship.
{Crew} practises juggling in the hold. Three apples become two apples and a lot of apple.
{Crew} writes the date on the galley wall, and one good thing that happened today. The wall is filling up.
{Crew} spends the session knitting something long and shapeless. It might be a scarf. It might be a snake.
{Crew} hums the same four notes all session. By the end, half the ship is humming them too.
{Crew} tidies the stash and finds a mitten everyone thought was lost on another world.

ship_life.text: {Crew} stays up long after everyone else, reading by a little lamp, perfectly content.
{Crew} has the kettle on and the lights up before anyone else is awake. The ship smells of toast.
{Crew} looks at a photo of home for a long time, then puts it away and joins the others for dinner.
{Crew} turns washing up into a timed contest and wins it, then demands a rematch with {crew.themself}.
{Crew} spends the whole session untangling one enormous knot of cable, one loop at a time, without a single sigh.
{Crew} trips over the same step for the third time this week and apologises to it.
{Crew} leaves a note that says "remember the thing". {Crew} does not remember the thing.
{Crew} whistles down every corridor. The ship feels a little brighter wherever {crew.they} {crew:goes|go}.
{Crew} narrates the making of a sandwich as if it were a great battle. The crew cheers at the end.
{Crew} reads the ship's manual for fun and finds a button nobody knew about. It turns on a tiny light. That is all it does.
{Crew} paces the whole ship end to end eleven times and finds three things that needed fixing on the way.
{Crew} cries a little at a sunset through the window, and says it is fine, it is just a very good sunset.
{Crew} reads a whole book in one sitting and spends the rest of the session staring at the wall, changed.
{Crew} challenges the ship's computer to chess and loses, and challenges it again.

arrive_crew: {Crew} is first to the window when {place} comes into view.

arrive_crew.text: {Crew} is out of the airlock before the ramp is all the way down.
{Crew} takes one look at {place} and starts drawing it.
{Crew} fills a sample jar before anyone else has their boots on.
{Crew} lifts {crew.their} {crew.gear} for a better look at the {biome}.

crew_pair: {Crew} and {other} split the last biscuit exactly in half. It takes a while.
{Crew} teaches {other} a card game. {Other} wins every round and pretends to be surprised.
{Crew} and {other} sit at the window and don't say much. They don't need to.
{Other} finds {crew} asleep at the console and puts a blanket over {crew.them}.
{Crew} and {other} argue about the best planet so far. Neither of them wins. Both of them enjoy it.

crew_pair.text: {Crew} and {other} are still polite with each other. Very polite. Extremely polite.
{Crew} asks {other} where {other.they} grew up. The answer takes all evening.
{Crew} and {other} have a joke now that nobody else understands. It involves a spoon.
{Crew} saves {other} the good mug without being asked. {Other} notices. {Other} always notices.
{Crew} and {other} finish each other's sentences now. It's a little annoying. Everyone loves it.
{Other} jumps at a noise, and {crew} is already there, laughing, holding out a cup of tea.
{Crew} grumbles about {other}'s humming. Later {crew} is caught humming the same tune.
{Crew} tells {other} the worst joke on the ship. {Other} laughs so hard {other.they} {other:has|have} to sit down.
{Crew} borrows {other}'s {other.gear} and gives it back slightly better than before.
{Crew} and {other} swap {crew.wear} and {other.wear} for a day, just to see. It suits them both.

crew_pair: {Crew} and {other} build a blanket fort in the galley and refuse to explain it.
{Crew} teaches {other} a card game with rules that keep changing. {Other} wins anyway.
{Crew} and {other} sit on the floor of the observation deck and talk about nothing for an hour.
{Crew} cuts {other}'s hair in the washroom. It is shorter on one side. They agree it is a look.
{Crew} and {other} race paper boats in the water tank. Both boats sink. They call it a draw.
{Crew} and {other} write a song together. It has one verse and nineteen choruses.
{Crew} helps {other} carry something heavy, and they keep talking long after it is put down.
{Crew} and {other} try to cook the same dish from two different recipes. Neither will admit the other one is better.
{Crew} reads aloud to {other} while {other} fixes something. Both jobs go better that way.
{Crew} and {other} watch a storm on the planet below from the window, and count the seconds between flashes.
{Crew} and {other} have an argument about the best season. It lasts all session and is very enjoyable.
{Crew} leaves {other} the last biscuit, and {other} pretends not to notice that it was on purpose.
postcard: Wish you were here. The view over the {biome} is even better than it sounds.
Greetings from {world}! The weather is {weather} and the crew is in a good mood.
{Crew} says hello. {Crew} also says the food here is very strange, in a good way.
Arrived safely. Nobody has fallen in anything yet. Fingers crossed.
Dear whoever reads this: we found a place called {world}. It's quiet, and we like it.
This is the view from the ship this morning. The photo doesn't do it justice. Nothing would.
{Crew} wanted to write something clever here. This is what we got.

postcard.text: It's freezing here. {Crew} hasn't taken off {crew.their} {crew.wear} in two days.
Hot, hot, hot. {Crew} is fanning {crew.themself} with this postcard as we speak.
So much water! {Crew} wants to learn to swim. We're not sure it's that kind of water.
There's life everywhere here. {Crew} keeps waving at things that might be waving back.
No ground at all, just clouds all the way down. {Crew} is pretending to be a bird.
